name: Barbell Incline Bench Press
summary: An upper-body barbell pressing exercise performed on an inclined bench to emphasize the upper chest and anterior shoulders.

setup: Set an adjustable bench to an incline between 30 and 45 degrees inside a rack or use an incline bench station.
Lie back on the bench with your feet planted firmly flat on the floor.
Retract and depress your shoulder blades, firmly pinning them into the backrest.
Grasp the barbell with a pronated grip slightly wider than shoulder width.
steps: Unrack the bar and hold it directly over your upper chest with elbows fully extended.
Lower the bar under control until it lightly touches your upper chest just below the clavicle.
Pause momentarily without letting the weight collapse onto your torso.
Press the bar upward and slightly backward along a smooth bar path back to the starting locked-out position.
instructions.breathing: Inhale deeply and brace your core as you lower the barbell, then exhale forcefully as you drive through the sticking point.
cues: Keep your shoulder blades pinched together.
Tuck elbows slightly rather than flaring them out wide.
Drive your feet through the floor for stability.

common_faults.fault: Setting the bench angle too steep (above 45 degrees).
common_faults.correction: Keep the bench angle around 30 to 45 degrees to target the upper chest instead of shifting the load entirely to the shoulders.

common_faults.fault: Excessively arching the lower back and lifting hips off the bench.
common_faults.correction: Maintain glute contact with the seat pad and keep an active core brace throughout the movement.

common_faults.fault: Flaring elbows directly out at a 90-degree angle to the torso.
common_faults.correction: Tuck elbows to roughly a 45- to 60-degree angle relative to the torso to protect the shoulder joints.

precautions: Ensure the bench angle is securely locked before loading.
Avoid bouncing the barbell off your chest.
